intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes
experiences.description: Hit the world-class slopes of the Jungfrau region, covering Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. With over 200km of marked runs suitable for all skill levels, families can enjoy beginner-friendly green runs while more experienced skiers tackle challenging red and black pistes. Ski school lessons are available for children and adults, making it perfect for family progression.

experiences.name: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure
experiences.description: Explore the stunning Aletsch Glacier area on a guided family snowshoeing tour. Walk through pristine snow-covered forests and open alpine meadows with breathtaking views of the longest glacier in the Alps. Guides provide all equipment and teach techniques suitable for children aged 6 and up, making it an accessible and memorable winter activity for the whole family.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, stretching over 3km with spectacular mountain scenery. Rent traditional wooden sleds and race down the illuminated night run for an unforgettable evening adventure. The run is suitable for children and adults alike, and the nearby mountain hut offers warm Swiss hot chocolate and raclette after the ride.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cogwheel railway to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, known as the Top of Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, visit the Sphinx Observatory, and enjoy panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier. The journey itself through tunnels and mountain stations is a thrilling experience for children, and the summit offers snow activities and a unique alpine restaurant for a memorable family lunch.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Cheese Culture Evening
experiences.description: Immerse the family in authentic Swiss mountain culture with a traditional fondue dinner at a historic mountain chalet. Learn about the centuries-old art of Swiss cheese-making, try your hand at fondue etiquette, and enjoy local specialties like raclette and rösti paired with warm apple cider for kids. Many chalets also offer folk music performances and yodeling demonstrations, giving families a genuine taste of alpine heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the SBB train from Zurich Airport to Interlaken Ost (approx. 2 hrs, ~CHF 30 with a Swiss Travel Pass or second-class ticket). From Interlaken Ost, take the Berner Oberland Bahn to Grindelwald (approx. 40 min, ~CHF 10). Check into your boutique accommodation in Grindelwald, freshen up, and take a short stroll through the village to get your bearings. Admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face from the village center — completely free!
day_by_day.evening: Explore Grindelwald village on foot. Visit the small local shops along the main street and pick up a trail map and ski pass information from the tourist office. Settle in and rest after your travel day.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick snack at Zurich Airport (budget CHF 8–12 for a sandwich and coffee)
meals.lunch: Grab a Migros or Coop supermarket meal deal at Zurich Airport or Interlaken station — sandwiches, yogurt, and juice for around CHF 10–12
meals.dinner: Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — a cozy, budget-friendly local restaurant offering Swiss classics like rösti and bratwurst for CHF 18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Jungfrau Ski Region ski pass as early as possible — multi-day passes offer the best value (6-day pass ~CHF 290 for adults). Consider buying a Half Fare Card (CHF 120) if you plan to use Swiss trains extensively — it pays off quickly. Confirm check-in time with your accommodation before arriving.

day_by_day.morning: First full ski day! Head to the Grindelwald-First ski area, accessible by gondola from the village center (included in Jungfrau Ski Region pass). Grindelwald-First offers wide, well-groomed blue and red runs ideal for all family skill levels. Start with the easier Schreckfeld and Bort runs to warm up. The gondola opens at 08:30 — arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the First plateau. Try the longer red runs from First (2,168m) down toward Bort. Take a mid-afternoon break at a mountain restaurant terrace to enjoy the panoramic views of the Wetterhorn and Schreckhorn peaks. Families with younger children can try the dedicated beginner slopes near Bort station.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by gondola (last descent around 16:30). Warm up with a hot chocolate at a village café. Rent or tune up ski equipment if needed at one of Grindelwald's many affordable rental shops (budget ~CHF 35–45/day for skis, boots, and poles).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your accommodation or self-cater with supermarket items (bread, cheese, cold cuts) — budget CHF 5–8
meals.lunch: Pack your own sandwiches and snacks from the Coop supermarket in the village to eat on the mountain — saves CHF 15–20 vs. mountain restaurant prices
meals.dinner: Restaurant Pizzeria Avocado in Grindelwald — offers hearty pizzas and pasta dishes for CHF 16–22 per person, popular with families

day_by_day.notes: Grindelwald-First is one of the most scenic and family-friendly ski areas in the Jungfrau region. Ski school lessons for children are available through Swiss Ski School Grindelwald (~CHF 45/half day). Always check avalanche bulletins at slf.ch before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Wengen train (Wengernalpbahn rack railway from Grindelwald Grund, ~CHF 12 one way or included in some passes) to Wengen village. From Wengen, access the Männlichen ski area via the Wengen-Männlichen gondola. Enjoy spectacular runs with unobstructed views of the Jungfrau, Mönch, and Eiger — the famous 'Big Three' peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the classic Männlichen–Kleine Scheidegg route — a long, scenic red run of about 7km that is one of the most famous ski descents in the Alps. Families can take the easier blue alternatives. Explore the Kleine Scheidegg area and consider a short snowshoe walk near the station (free, no equipment needed beyond warm boots).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald via train from Kleine Scheidegg (Wengernalpbahn). Visit the Grindelwald Sports Centre for a relaxed evening skate on the outdoor ice rink (~CHF 8 admission + CHF 5 skate rental) — a perfect family activity.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at accommodation — oatmeal, fruit, and hot drinks (budget CHF 4–6)
meals.lunch: Restaurant at Kleine Scheidegg station — try the self-service section for soup and bread at around CHF 12–15, more affordable than table service
meals.dinner: Coop supermarket dinner — pick up ready-made meals, cheese fondue kits, or fresh ingredients to cook at accommodation if kitchen facilities are available (budget CHF 12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Männlichen–Kleine Scheidegg run is a bucket-list ski experience. On clear days, the views are absolutely extraordinary. Wednesday tends to be less crowded than weekends. Check if your ski pass covers the Wengen-Männlichen gondola — some Jungfrau passes include it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Jungfraujoch — 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m. Take the train from Grindelwald Grund via Kleine Scheidegg to Jungfraujoch (round trip ~CHF 145 adult, CHF 72.50 with Half Fare Card — book in advance online for Good Morning Ticket discounts of ~25%). Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory viewing deck, and the eternal snow plateau. This is the highlight of the entire trip!
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the full afternoon at Jungfraujoch. Walk on the Aletsch Glacier (supervised area), try the snow disc sledging near the plateau, and take photos at Europe's highest railway station. Visit the Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven exhibition (included in ticket). Begin descent by 15:00 to avoid the evening rush.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by 17:00. Rest your legs — Jungfraujoch can cause mild altitude fatigue. Enjoy a quiet evening in the village. Browse the local souvenir shops for affordable Swiss chocolates and postcards.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation — depart by 07:30 to catch the Good Morning discount train (must arrive at Jungfraujoch before 10:00)
meals.lunch: Self Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — budget option with soup, bread, and hot drinks for CHF 15–20. Alternatively, bring packed lunch from the village to save money (eating areas available)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Mercato in Grindelwald — Swiss and international dishes, good value set menus around CHF 20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch tickets well in advance at jungfrau.ch — the Good Morning Ticket saves significant money. Dress in VERY warm layers — temperatures at the top can be -15°C or colder with wind chill. This is a non-skiing day but arguably the most memorable experience of the trip. Children under 16 travel free with a paying adult on Swiss Federal Railways.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Kleine Scheidegg ski area for a full day of skiing. Access via the Wengernalpbahn rack railway from Grindelwald Grund. The runs around Kleine Scheidegg and Lauberhorn are world-famous — this is where the annual Lauberhorn World Cup downhill race takes place. Try the Lauberhorn run itself (a long red, 4.5km) for an exhilarating experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, try tobogganing on the Grindelwald–Bussalp toboggan run — one of the longest natural toboggan runs in the Bernese Oberland at 6km (toboggan rental ~CHF 10, run access free). The run starts at Bussalp (reachable by post bus from Grindelwald) and finishes back in the village. Perfect for the whole family!
day_by_day.evening: Warm up at the Sunstar Hotel's public après-ski bar area in Grindelwald — enjoy a hot Glühwein (mulled wine, ~CHF 6) or hot chocolate in a lively but relaxed atmosphere. Browse the weekly local market if running (check locally).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation (bread, jam, cheese, coffee) — budget CHF 4–6
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and thermoses of hot soup from accommodation to eat on the mountain or at toboggan run
meals.dinner: Pizzeria-Restaurant Espresso in Grindelwald — casual, family-friendly, pizzas and pasta from CHF 15–20 per person. Great value for families.

day_by_day.notes: The Grindelwald–Bussalp toboggan run is a fantastic, affordable family activity and a welcome break from skiing. Check post bus schedules to Bussalp at postauto.ch. Friday afternoons can get busier on slopes as weekend visitors begin arriving — consider an early start on the mountain.

day_by_day.morning: Final full ski day — make the most of it! Return to your favorite ski area from the week. Alternatively, explore the Grindelwald-First area's non-ski winter activities: the First Cliff Walk (a dramatic cliffside walkway at 2,168m, free with gondola ticket) offers stunning views even in winter when accessible. Check conditions locally.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try a guided snowshoe tour departing from Grindelwald village — organized tours run by local guides cost ~CHF 25–35 per person including snowshoe rental. Routes through the Grindelwald valley offer incredible views of the Eiger and are suitable for families with children aged 6+. Alternatively, spend the afternoon on beginner slopes for younger family members to consolidate skills.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Grindelwald. Treat yourself to a proper Swiss fondue experience — a fitting end to an Alpine holiday. Many restaurants offer fondue sets for groups.

meals.breakfast: Slightly more indulgent breakfast — visit the local Bäckerei (bakery) for fresh croissants, Gipfeli, and coffee for CHF 8–10 per person
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant treat — budget CHF 18–22 for a hot meal such as Älplermagronen (Swiss Alpine mac and cheese) or Käseschnitte (cheese toast) at a mountain hut
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte or Hotel Belvedere's restaurant — traditional Swiss cheese fondue for CHF 25–32 per person. Order the classic moitié-moitié (half Gruyère, half Vacherin). Book ahead on Saturday evenings!

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day on the slopes as weekly visitors are replaced by weekend visitors. Head out very early (before 09:00) to get the best snow and avoid lift queues. Return ski rental equipment today if renting — most shops require returns by 18:00. Pack bags this evening to make Sunday morning departure smooth.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of accommodation (typically by 10:00 — confirm with hotel). Store luggage at the hotel or Grindelwald station left-luggage facility. Take one last walk through Grindelwald village and along the valley floor trail toward the Glacier Gorge viewpoint (Gletscherschlucht) — a short, scenic 30-minute walk that is free in winter. Enjoy the crisp mountain air and final views of the Eiger one last time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train from Grindelwald back to Interlaken Ost (40 min), then connect to Interlaken West or Bern for onward travel. If time allows before your departure train, stop in Interlaken for a quick browse of the main shopping street (Höheweg) for last-minute Swiss chocolate and souvenir purchases — Coop and Migros have excellent affordable Swiss chocolate selections. Board your train to Zurich Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport with plenty of time before your return flight. Enjoy a final Swiss meal or snack at the airport. Safe travels home!

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at accommodation if included, or grab fresh pastries and coffee from a village bakery for CHF 8–10
meals.lunch: Migros or Coop at Interlaken station — grab sandwiches, fruit, and drinks for the journey (CHF 10–14). Good value and convenient for travel days.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich — budget CHF 20–30 for a meal at one of the more affordable airport restaurants, or bring snacks purchased at Coop/Migros for the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours from Grindelwald to Zurich Airport including train connections and airport check-in. The Grindelwald–Interlaken–Zurich Airport route is well-served by SBB trains on Sundays. Double-check train times at sbb.ch the night before. Keep receipts for any Swiss VAT refunds on purchases over CHF 300 (refundable at the airport). Total estimated budget for the 7-day trip per adult: CHF 600–850 excluding flights and accommodation (ski pass ~CHF 290, food ~CHF 200, transport ~CHF 100, activities ~CHF 100–200).

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel from the airport (Zurich or Geneva) to Grindelwald via train. The scenic rail journey takes approximately 2.5–3 hours and passes through stunning Swiss countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Boutique Stay in Grindelwald-Wengen by mid-afternoon. Check in, unpack, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through Grindelwald village. Browse the local ski rental shops along the main street to arrange equipment for the week ahead and pick up any necessary lift passes.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the hotel or a nearby traditional Swiss restaurant in Grindelwald village. Try a hearty rösti or a mountain soup to warm up after the journey.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at the airport/train station
meals.lunch: Light bite at a train station café or on-board the train — pick up a sandwich and Swiss chocolate from a Migros or Coop kiosk
meals.dinner: Restaurant Alte Post or similar mid-range village restaurant in Grindelwald — budget CHF 30–45 per adult for a main course and drink

day_by_day.notes: Priority on arrival day: confirm ski rental and lift pass bookings for the week to avoid queues. The Grindelwald tourist office near the train station can assist with passes and local maps. Dress warmly — February temperatures in Grindelwald typically range from -5°C to +3°C.

day_by_day.morning: First full skiing day on the Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes. Head to the Grindelwald-First gondola or the Männlichen cable car for a morning session on wide, beginner-to-intermediate groomed runs. Families with younger children can start on the gentle slopes near the base, while stronger skiers can explore the upper mountain terrain above 2,000m.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Jungfrau Ski Region, exploring the interconnected runs linking Grindelwald and Wengen. Take a mid-afternoon break at one of the mountain restaurants — Bergrestaurant Männlichen offers panoramic Eiger views and hearty lunches. Return to the base by 16:00 to allow time to rest.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Grindelwald village on foot. Visit the small local shops for Swiss souvenirs and chocolate. Enjoy a family-friendly dinner at a village restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — included or CHF 15–20 supplement; enjoy muesli, fresh bread, cheese, and cold cuts
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant on the slopes — try a Bergstube soup bowl and Bratwurst with bread, budget CHF 20–30 per person
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter or Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — mid-range pizza, pasta, and Swiss dishes, CHF 25–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski equipment the evening before (Day 1) to save time on the first ski day. Purchase the Jungfrau Ski Region pass for multiple days to get the best value — a 6-day adult pass costs approximately CHF 330–370. Children under 9 often ski free with a paying adult.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure — join a guided family snowshoeing tour in the Aletsch Glacier area. The tour departs from Grindelwald or a nearby valley and leads through pristine winter landscapes with breathtaking views of the UNESCO World Heritage glacier. Guides provide all equipment and safety briefings suitable for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the snowshoeing tour concludes, return to Grindelwald by early afternoon. Spend time at the hotel to rest and warm up with hot chocolate. Alternatively, visit the Grindelwald Sports Centre for an indoor skating session — a fun and easy activity for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Cheese Culture Evening — immerse the family in authentic Swiss mountain culture with a traditional fondue dinner at a historic chalet restaurant. This is a highlight experience combining entertainment, storytelling about Swiss cheese-making traditions, and delicious food.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up well before the snowshoeing adventure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator or a simple café stop in the valley — light sandwiches and warm drinks, CHF 15–20 per person
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Cheese Culture Evening experience — typically CHF 45–65 per adult including fondue, bread, and a drink; children's portions available

day_by_day.notes: Book the Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure and the Fondue Evening in advance — both are popular experiences that fill up quickly in peak February season. Wear waterproof trousers and sturdy boots for snowshoeing. The fondue evening is an excellent cultural highlight and highly recommended for families.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion — depart early from Grindelwald station to catch the cogwheel railway up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters. The journey itself is spectacular, passing through the Eiger's north face tunnel with viewing windows. At the top, explore the Ice Palace, the Sphinx Observatory, and the year-round snow plateau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — try a short guided walk on the snow plateau, take family photos with the iconic summit backdrop, and visit the interactive Alpine Sensation exhibition inside the mountain. Begin the descent by 14:30 to avoid late afternoon crowds, returning to Grindelwald by 16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel or village. Take a gentle evening walk through the illuminated village streets. Opt for an early, lighter dinner to recover from the high altitude.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — depart by 08:00 for best experience at the top
meals.lunch: Restaurant Crystal at Jungfraujoch — self-service buffet with hot meals at altitude; budget CHF 25–35 per person; alternatively bring packed snacks to save costs
meals.dinner: Café 3692 or Pizzeria da Salvi in Grindelwald village — relaxed mid-range dining, CHF 25–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — February is peak season and tickets sell out. Adult return fare is approximately CHF 145–155 with the Swiss Travel Pass discount; children under 16 receive significant discounts. Dress in warm layers — temperatures at the summit can reach -15°C or lower with wind chill. Altitude sickness is possible; stay hydrated and ascend slowly.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes for a second skiing day, this time exploring the Wengen side of the ski area. Take the train from Grindelwald to Wengen (a scenic 15-minute ride) and access the Lauberhorn slopes — famous for hosting the annual World Cup downhill race. Intermediate and advanced skiers will love the long, classic runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski down to Wengen village for a leisurely lunch, then continue afternoon skiing on the lower Wengen and Männlichen slopes. Families with beginners can use the gentler blue runs near Wengen village. Finish skiing by 15:30 and take the scenic train back to Grindelwald.
day_by_day.evening: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run (or the nearby Grindelwald-First toboggan run if Fläsch is not accessible same day) — experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, stretching over 3km. Evening toboggan sessions are often available and are magical under the winter stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Wengen village restaurant — Restaurant Hirschen or similar, traditional Swiss mountain lunch with rösti and soup, CHF 20–35 per person
meals.dinner: Self-catered or light meal at a local Grindelwald bakery/takeaway — pick up raclette rolls, pretzels, and hot drinks to enjoy after tobogganing, CHF 10–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Tobogganing sleds can be rented at the top of the run for approximately CHF 10–15. Check evening toboggan run availability and opening hours in advance as they vary by day. The run is suitable for children aged 5 and above. Wear a helmet (available for rental) and waterproof clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning — choose based on energy levels and family preference. Options include: a final morning ski session on the Grindelwald-First area, a leisurely snowshoe walk on a self-guided trail near the village, or a relaxed morning at the hotel with a late breakfast and spa time (if available at the boutique stay).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Grindelwald Glacier Gorge (Gletscherschlucht) — a short walk from the village centre. The frozen gorge is a dramatic natural spectacle in winter, with ice formations and towering rock walls. Entry is approximately CHF 5–8 per person. Afterwards, spend time shopping for Swiss souvenirs, watches, and local products along the main street.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell family dinner at one of Grindelwald's best mid-range restaurants. Celebrate the week with a special three-course Swiss meal featuring alpine specialties like cheese soup, venison, and apple strudel.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — enjoy a slower morning
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local Grindelwald café — try a Zopf bread sandwich and hot chocolate, CHF 12–18 per person
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte or Hotel Kirchbühl restaurant in Grindelwald — three-course Swiss alpine dinner, CHF 45–65 per adult; children's menu available

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in peak season can be busy in the village as weekly changeover guests arrive. Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance. Use the afternoon to pack ski equipment for return and prepare for departure. Consider purchasing Swiss chocolate, cheese, and local jams as gifts — the Migros supermarket in the village offers good value.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps. Enjoy a leisurely last hotel breakfast and take a short scenic walk through Grindelwald for final photos of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau peaks. Check out of the boutique stay by the required time (typically 11:00).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Grindelwald by train towards Zurich or Geneva airport. The scenic rail journey offers a beautiful final view of the Bernese Oberland mountains. Allow at least 3–3.5 hours travel time to the airport plus 2 hours for check-in. Stop at Bern or Interlaken station briefly if time allows for a final Swiss coffee or pastry.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight — travel home with wonderful memories of the Swiss Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy it fully before checkout
meals.lunch: Train station or airport dining — Coop or Migros at Interlaken Ost or Bern station for affordable sandwiches, CHF 10–15 per person
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on-board the return flight

day_by_day.notes: Sunday trains in Switzerland run on a reliable schedule but can be busy with weekend travellers. Book train tickets in advance via SBB.ch for the best fares. Leave extra time if travelling with ski bags or large luggage — some trains require advance reservation for oversized baggage. Grindelwald to Zurich Airport takes approximately 2.5–3 hours; to Geneva Airport approximately 3–3.5 hours.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00; no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from the airport to Boutique Stay in Grindelwald-Wengen, Jungfrau Region (approx. 2.5–3 hours via chauffeured Mercedes V-Class or helicopter transfer upgrade available).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hotel Check-In & Orientation — Arrive at the boutique property mid-afternoon. Meet your dedicated concierge, receive a full property tour, and settle into your suite. Take a leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village to acclimatize to the altitude and crisp mountain air. Browse the charming alpine shops along the main promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome Dinner at the Hotel — Enjoy a private welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant or a curated table at Restaurant Schmitte (Grindelwald), known for its refined Swiss-Alpine cuisine. Toast the trip with a Swiss Chasselas white wine or local Valais Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: N/A — In-flight or airport dining prior to arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge dining pre-departure; alternatively a charcuterie and cheese board upon arrival at the hotel
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte or hotel signature dining — multi-course alpine menu featuring air-dried Bündnerfleisch, wild mushroom risotto, and slow-roasted veal with rösti

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in if available. Consider a helicopter transfer from Zurich or Bern for a dramatic alpine arrival experience. Altitude in Grindelwald is approx. 1,034m — light activity on Day 1 is recommended for families with young children.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes — Begin your alpine ski adventure on the world-class slopes of the Jungfrau Ski Region covering Grindelwald and Wengen. Arrange private ski instruction through the Swiss Ski School for all family members. Collect premium rental equipment (Rossignol or Völkl) from the on-slope boutique rental shop. Start on the First or Männlichen sector for stunning Eiger views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continued Skiing & Mountain Lunch — Progress to more varied runs across the Grindelwald-Wengen sector. Take the Gondelbahn Grindelwald-Männlichen for panoramic ridge-top skiing. Enjoy a long afternoon session before the lifts close, with a mid-afternoon hot chocolate break at a mountain hut.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Cheese Culture Evening — Immerse the family in authentic Swiss mountain culture with a traditional fondue dinner at a historic alpine chalet. Experience cheese fondue, raclette, and Rösti alongside local storytelling and live accordion music. A truly memorable family evening.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast buffet at the hotel — freshly baked Zopf bread, local cheeses, cold cuts, bircher muesli, and hot chocolate for the children
meals.lunch: Restaurant Grindelwaldblick on the mountain — panoramic terrace lunch with alpine macaroni (Älplermagronen), bratwurst, and warm apple strudel
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue & Cheese Culture Evening — traditional three-cheese fondue, charcuterie platter, and Swiss wine pairing at a historic alpine chalet restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Book private ski instructors at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge. Helmets and appropriate layering are essential. The fondue evening experience typically includes transport to and from the chalet — confirm pickup time with the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion — Depart early from Grindelwald station on the iconic cogwheel railway to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, the highest railway station in Europe. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, the Sphinx Observatory, and the Ice Palace. Allow approximately 2.5–3 hours for the round journey and exploration at the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exploration at the Summit & Return — Spend the afternoon at Jungfraujoch exploring the Snow Fun Park (snowtubing, zip-line over the glacier), the Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven exhibit, and the breathtaking Plateau viewing terrace. Descend back to Grindelwald by mid-afternoon with time to rest at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Spa & Wellness Evening — Unwind at the hotel's luxury spa facilities after an exhilarating day at altitude. Enjoy couples' or family relaxation treatments, an alpine herbal bath, and the heated indoor pool. Children can enjoy the dedicated kids' spa menu (warm milk baths, gentle massage).

meals.breakfast: Early à la carte breakfast at the hotel before departure — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch (3,454m) — self-service alpine lunch with panoramic glacier views; try the Top of Europe soup and Swiss cheese platter
meals.dinner: In-hotel fine dining — four-course tasting menu at the hotel restaurant featuring Valais lamb, truffle risotto, and a Swiss chocolate dessert selection

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm, windproof layers — temperatures at Jungfraujoch can drop to -15°C or below. Book Jungfraujoch train tickets in advance (Good Morning Ticket available for early departures at reduced rates). Children under 16 often travel free or at reduced fares. Allow time for acclimatization at the top — altitude sickness is possible; move slowly and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Snowshoeing Adventure — Join a guided family snowshoeing tour through the pristine landscapes near the Aletsch Glacier area. A certified mountain guide leads the group through snow-covered forests and open glacier plateaus. Suitable for all fitness levels and ages — snowshoes and poles provided. Duration approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tobogganing on the Fläsch Run — Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, stretching over 3km of exhilarating descents. The Fläsch Run near Grindelwald offers breathtaking scenery and pure family fun. Multiple runs available throughout the afternoon. A private guide can be arranged for safety briefings and the best lines.
day_by_day.evening: Private Fondue Carriage Ride — Arrange through the concierge a horse-drawn sleigh ride through the snowy Grindelwald valley at dusk, ending at a private alpine farmhouse for a candlelit dinner with local farmers' cheese, cured meats, and mulled wine (Glühwein) for adults and warm spiced apple juice for children.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — warm porridge with Swiss honey and dried fruits, fresh croissants, and a selection of local mountain cheeses and jams
meals.lunch: Picnic-style mountain lunch prepared by the hotel — insulated flask of tomato soup, artisan sandwiches on Graubünden rye bread, Swiss chocolate bars, and thermos of hot tea
meals.dinner: Private alpine farmhouse dinner — farmer's cheese board, house-cured meats, hearty bean soup, and homemade apple tart with cream

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoeing guide should be booked through the hotel concierge or Swiss Mountain Guide Association. Waterproof trousers and gaiters are recommended for snowshoeing. The horse-drawn sleigh and farmhouse dinner is a premium add-on that must be reserved 2–3 days in advance — your concierge can arrange this exclusively.

day_by_day.morning: Advanced Skiing Day — Wengen Sector — Take the train from Grindelwald to Wengen (car-free village) for a fresh skiing perspective. Explore the legendary Lauberhorn race piste — one of the most famous downhill courses in the world. Hire a private mountain guide to access off-piste powder fields safely. Stunning views of the Eiger North Face throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski Safari to Mürren — Continue the ski safari via cable car connections to reach Mürren, the dramatic cliff-top village with views across to the Schilthorn. Ski the Schilthorn sector and visit the 007 Piz Gloria revolving restaurant (made famous by James Bond's 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service'). Return to Grindelwald via the valley train.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Spa Treatment & Gala Dinner — Return to the hotel for pre-booked luxury spa treatments: hot stone massage for adults, children's relaxation session. Dress for a special gala-style dinner at one of Grindelwald's finest restaurants — Restaurant Firestarter or The Capricorn, offering modern Alpine cuisine with international flair.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in-suite or at the hotel — freshly baked viennoiseries, smoked salmon, poached eggs, and a glass of Prosecco for adults
meals.lunch: Piz Gloria Revolving Restaurant at Schilthorn (2,970m) — panoramic 360° lunch with Swiss rösti, mountain herb soup, and Toblerone fondue dessert
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter or The Capricorn, Grindelwald — modern alpine tasting menu: beetroot-cured salmon, slow-cooked Simmental beef fillet, and a Swiss chocolate sphere dessert with warm praline sauce

day_by_day.notes: The ski safari from Wengen to Mürren is an ambitious day — confirm snow and lift conditions the evening before with your guide. The Schilthorn cable car from Mürren is a separate ticket. Piz Gloria lunch reservations should be made in advance. Dress smartly for the evening gala dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Private Ice Skating & Winter Village Experience — Enjoy a relaxed morning at the natural outdoor ice rink in Grindelwald (or the indoor rink if weather is poor). Private skating lessons can be arranged for younger children. Afterwards, explore the Grindelwald Christmas market-style winter village stalls for artisan Swiss gifts, local honey, and handmade wooden toys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Helicopter Mountain Tour — Treat the family to a breathtaking private helicopter scenic flight over the Jungfrau massif, Aletsch Glacier, and surrounding peaks. Approximately 30–45 minutes, departing from Grindelwald helipad. Land on a remote glacier plateau for a champagne toast before returning. A once-in-a-lifetime experience for the entire family.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Swiss Cheese & Wine Tasting — Host a private in-suite or hotel cellar cheese and wine tasting curated by the hotel sommelier. Sample 6–8 Swiss AOC cheeses (Gruyère, Appenzeller, Raclette du Valais, Emmental, Sbrinz, and Vacherin Fribourgeois) paired with Swiss Fendant, Humagne Rouge, and Pinot Noir. Children enjoy a chocolate and Swiss juice pairing.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — full Swiss spread with regional specialties, fresh fruit platters, and warm pastries
meals.lunch: Restaurant Alte Post, Grindelwald — traditional Swiss lunch in a historic 1875 alpine inn; try the Berner Platte (smoked meats, sausages, sauerkraut) or the classic cheese soup
meals.dinner: Private in-suite or cellar farewell dinner — curated cheese and charcuterie feast followed by a decadent chocolate fondue dessert with seasonal fruits and Swiss meringues

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours must be booked at least 3–4 days in advance and are subject to weather conditions — always have a backup plan. The hotel concierge can arrange glacier landing permits and champagne service on the snow. The cheese and wine tasting can be arranged as a private event in the hotel's wine cellar for a truly intimate experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning Ski Run or Leisure Walk — For keen skiers, enjoy one last morning on the slopes for a final run down a favorite piste before equipment return. Alternatively, take a gentle guided snowshoe walk through the Grindelwald valley floor, stopping at a traditional alpine dairy farm to watch cheese being made and sample fresh Gruyère.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-Out & Departure Transfer — Complete hotel check-out after a leisurely lunch. Private luxury transfer (chauffeured vehicle or helicopter) departs Grindelwald for Zurich Airport or your onward destination. Allow 3 hours for road transfer to Zurich. Final views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau as you depart the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Flight home or onward journey. Airport lounge access recommended (Swiss Business Lounge at Zurich Airport) for a comfortable send-off.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — special farewell spread with a selection of the week's highlights: cheese board, bircher muesli, warm pastries, and fresh-pressed alpine herb juice
meals.lunch: Restaurant Kreuz & Post, Grindelwald — beloved local institution serving traditional Swiss lunch; try the rösti with fried egg and smoked bacon, or the hearty Älplermagronen
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — Swiss Business Class meal service or Swiss Lounge dining at Zurich Airport

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-out (2:00 PM) through the hotel concierge if your transfer allows. Ensure all ski rental equipment is returned by 11:00 AM to avoid additional charges. Purchase last-minute Swiss gifts at the hotel boutique or Grindelwald village shops before departure — local honey, Lindt chocolate, and Swiss army knives make excellent souvenirs. Confirm transfer booking the night before departure.
